posts.text:
We have a mandate from the people to fight for bold, transformative policy.

If you want to hear more about what I'm fighting for, sign up for my Congressional newsletter:

https://t.co/0rp0Mrdvts

We need to show people what Democrats can do with our majority.

Reparations. Abortion justice. Medicare for All. Abolishing ICE. Childcare. Paid leave. And more.

If Trump wants to veto any of this, then the people will know exactly where he stands. And we won’t stop fighting https://t.co/UhE00pRiQR

The Black unemployment rate in America is still a crisis and we're not done sounding the alarm.

It has consequences for Black families and futures, but the harm is coming for all of us.

The Fed must uphold its mandate for maximum employment and confront this crisis head-on.

Earlier this week, Mother Randle turned 112 years old.

Mother Randle is a mother, grandmother, a civil rights movement pioneer, & the last known living survivor of the Tulsa Race Massacre.

She has dedicated her whole life to calling for reparations for the atrocity that happened in Greenwood—and we must fulfill this essential need for repair.

Reparations is racial justice, economic justice, & a moral imperative. It is deeply necessary to confront America’s damning history of systemic racism—and that includes the Tulsa Race Massacre.

That’s why in Congress I’m pushing to enact reparations and pass H.R. 40, establishing a pathway towards truth & repair for survivors like Mother Randle.

Under this new Democratic majority, I’ll keep pushing for reparations because we’re not backing down in our pursuit of healing & reparative justice.

The Black unemployment rate in America is still a crisis and we're not done sounding the alarm.

It has consequences for Black families and futures, but the harm is coming for all of us.

The Fed must uphold its mandate for maximum employment and confront this crisis head-on.

Earlier this week, Mother Randle turned 112 years old.

Mother Randle is a mother, grandmother, a civil rights movement pioneer, & the last known living survivor of the Tulsa Race Massacre.

She has dedicated her whole life to calling for reparations for the atrocity that happened in Greenwood—and we must fulfill this essential need for repair.

Reparations is racial justice, economic justice, & a moral imperative. It is deeply necessary to confront America’s damning history of systemic racism—and that includes the Tulsa Race Massacre.

That’s why in Congress I’m pushing to enact reparations and pass H.R. 40, establishing a pathway towards truth & repair for survivors like Mother Randle.

Under this new Democratic majority, I’ll keep pushing for reparations because we’re not backing down in our pursuit of healing & reparative justice.
